key_points: Dorm system is central to campus community and social life.
Weekly masses and events create strong dorm-based belonging.
Five Corners Apartments offer an off-campus housing alternative.
Football is the dominant social force unifying the campus.
Campus culture is tight-knit, warm, and genuinely welcoming.
Club sports and dorm activities provide non-varsity social outlets.
Almost no student commentary exists on dining quality or options.
Dining locations like LaFun and Duncan offer campus jobs.
Insufficient data to meaningfully assess dining experience.
Free counseling is available through the University Counseling Center.
System appears equipped to handle mental health crises directly.
Some cultural dismissiveness around mental health concerns is present.
Notre Dame is now need-blind for all students including internationals.
Middle-class families frequently fall into a painful financial aid gap.
International students on full rides get ~$1,000 flight reimbursement.
ACMS major sits awkwardly between CS and pure math job markets.
Aerospace engineering and dual-degree programs are well-regarded by students.
Some programs rely on outdated marketing to oversell job prospects.
Admissions office is known for compassionate, thoughtful rejection letters.
International financial aid requires navigating specific forms with strict timing.
NROTC waitlist coordination requires direct outreach; not well-integrated.
Campus aesthetics are consistently rated S or A tier by students.
The Golden Dome is a genuine source of student pride.
South Bend is quiet with little activity beyond Notre Dame life.
Notre Dame is a recognized strong pipeline into finance careers.
General prestige and alumni network are seen as major assets.
Niche interdisciplinary majors may not translate cleanly to employer recognition.
With strong aid, Notre Dame costs can rival in-state tuition.
Middle-class families at full sticker price face serious affordability hardship.
New need-blind policy may improve value for lower-income students.
Campus culture centers on football, faith, and strong institutional pride.
Non-Catholics and atheists report feeling genuinely welcome on campus.
Quiet Midwestern location may not suit students wanting urban energy.
Academics: ACMS job market pitched with outdated 2009 marketing materials.
Safety: Notre Dame named in documentary on mishandled assault claims.
Financial Aid: Middle-class families often too rich for aid, too poor for tuition.
International full-aid students get ~$1,000 flight reimbursement and Target gift card.
Club sports offer community and play without varsity-level time commitment.
Notably kind rejection letters reflect genuine warmth in institutional character.
